title: Mary and Protestants
hookLine: Protestants honor Mary in their own ways; Luther wrote a commentary on the Magnificat

lines: MY SOUL DOTH MAGNIFY THE LORD.
THE SAME SONG IN TWO CHURCHES.
cards: "My soul doth magnify the Lord." Late in the afternoon, in an old English cathedral, a choir in white robes stands to sing those words. It's Evensong, the evening prayer of the Church of England, and the words are Mary's.
The same evening, in a Catholic monastery, monks sing the same song at Vespers, in Latin, beginning Magnificat. Two buildings, two churches, one young woman's song rising at dusk.
People sometimes assume Mary belongs only to Catholics and the Orthodox, and that Protestants leave her out. The evening tells a more interesting story.

teach.h: ALL GENERATIONS SHALL CALL ME BLESSED.
teach.b: You learned Mary's song back in year one.
In Luke's Gospel, Mary visits her cousin Elizabeth and answers her greeting with a song. In the Douay-Rheims: "for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed."
Luke is in Catholic and Protestant Bibles alike, so calling Mary blessed is scripture. Second, Martin Luther. The same reformer who broke with Rome wrote a whole commentary on the Magnificat.
He held it up as a lesson in how God looks on the lowly: Mary, a girl of no standing, chosen and lifted up, and the proud scattered. In it, Luther calls her the Mother of God. Third, the prayer book.
The Church of England's Book of Common Prayer sets the Magnificat in Evening Prayer, so Anglicans sing at dusk: "My soul doth magnify the Lord : and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour."

Fourth, the honest differences. Catholics and Orthodox Christians ask Mary to pray for them, and Catholics hold teachings about her, like the Immaculate Conception, that Protestant churches don't share.

teach.h: WHERE CHURCHES DIFFER, AND WHERE THEY MEET.
teach.b: Protestant churches differ among themselves too: some keep feasts of Mary; some honor her as a model of faith and listening, and pray to God without asking for her prayers.

teach.h: MY SOUL DOTH MAGNIFY THE LORD.
teach.b: The Second Vatican Council spoke with joy of other Christians who honor the Mother of the Lord. So Mary isn't only a fence line. She's a place where people who disagree about a great deal still sing the same words.

how: Catholics sing or say the Magnificat at Vespers, the Church's evening prayer; Anglicans sing it at Evening Prayer (Evensong) from the Book of Common Prayer, and Lutherans also use it at evening services.

games.q: you're Mary. your cousin Elizabeth has just greeted you as blessed among women. what do you do?
games.why: she sings: "my soul doth magnify the Lord." the song is still sung at dusk, by Catholics at Vespers and by Anglicans at Evensong.

practice: If you pray, say slowly, the way choirs do at dusk: "My soul doth magnify the Lord." Breathe, and then: "And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour."
If you don't pray, simply hold the picture of two churches across a city, the same song going up from both at evening, and let the people in them be neighbors for a minute.
